episode.title: Keep terminal fast-echo optimization on an ASCII-safe boundary
episode.before: At parent d5416284f11ccbc735c8357f0ab35ce5f683ccc3, the text input's direct-to-stdout append shortcut admitted text whenever stringWidth(text) equaled JavaScript text.length, and its direct backspace shortcut admitted any final grapheme whose display width was one cell. Those shape checks allowed width-one non-ASCII input, including precomposed Vietnamese IME output, to bypass the normal Ink render path, risking divergence among displayed cells, stored input, and cursor position.
episode.after: At 9fb40e6a3d6338b6a6a616010de7a16672148924, direct append and backspace are permitted only when the affected text is nonempty printable ASCII and the existing end-of-line, single-line, non-wrapping, focused-TTY conditions also hold. Non-ASCII, combining, wide, emoji, control, multiline, middle-edit, and wrap-boundary cases fall through to normal rendering. Exported pure eligibility helpers make this boundary directly testable.
episode.diff: The change adds a printable-ASCII predicate and two pure fast-path eligibility helpers, replaces the prior display-width equality checks at both stdout bypass call sites with those helpers, preserves the existing direct stdout writes and deferred synchronization for eligible ASCII edits, and adds a focused 19-test regression matrix covering accepted ASCII plus rejected Vietnamese, combining-mark, CJK, emoji, control, NBSP/Latin-1, cursor-position, multiline, empty-input, and wrapping cases.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 9fb40e6a is the implementation-bearing resolution for issue/PR 26011, with parent d5416284, and changes only the text-input implementation and a new focused test file.

The parent implementation admitted append text when stringWidth(text) equaled text.length and admitted backspace when the removed grapheme's stringWidth was one, in addition to the common fast-echo base and line-shape conditions.
Before the change, successful append and backspace eligibility caused direct stdout writes and commits that skipped immediate local and parent synchronization.
The new append eligibility helper requires the cursor at the end, a nonempty single-line value, printable ASCII inserted text, and a resulting line width strictly below the terminal column count.
The new backspace eligibility helper requires deletion at the end of a nonempty single-line value and admits the removed grapheme only when it consists entirely of printable ASCII.
The component combines the existing focused, unmasked, unselected TTY precondition with the new pure helpers before selecting the direct append or backspace paths.
Eligible ASCII edits retain the optimized direct stdout behavior, while failed eligibility falls through to the ordinary edit and render flow.
Append tests preserve the intended ASCII fast path and reject unsafe structural states: cursor not at end, empty placeholder state, multiline input, and an append reaching the wrap column.
Append regression tests reject precomposed Vietnamese letters, Vietnamese tone-mark letters, NFD combining marks, CJK, emoji, ANSI/control text, NBSP, and Latin-1 letters.
Backspace tests preserve deletion of a final ASCII character and reject middle-of-line or empty deletion, multiline values, Vietnamese, CJK, NFD-composed graphemes, and emoji.
The patch extracts pure eligibility helpers, replaces the two width-based guards, and adds the dedicated fast-echo regression suite without redesigning the normal renderer.

The commit message reports that the regression matrix was red under the previous guard for 11 of 20 checked cases and green under the new guard; this is author-reported validation rather than a test execution performed during extraction.

The implementation explains that display-width equality is insufficient because a precomposed Vietnamese character can have both length one and width one while still participating in multi-keystroke IME composition.

candidate_atomics.name: gate-direct-append-by-safe-terminal-text
candidate_atomics.title: Restrict direct terminal append to layout-stable text
candidate_atomics.description: Replace a permissive width-equality test with an explicit eligibility contract that allows direct terminal append only for printable ASCII in an end-of-line, single-line, non-wrapping state.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent composed, combining, wide, ambiguous, or control input from bypassing the renderer while retaining low-latency direct echo for ordinary ASCII typing.
semantic_action.pre_state: A direct-to-terminal append optimization is selected using display-width and code-unit equality, so some width-one non-ASCII or composition-related text can be treated as layout-stable.
semantic_action.post_state: Direct append is eligible only when runtime TTY conditions hold and the edit is printable ASCII at the end of a nonempty single-line value without reaching the wrap boundary; all other text uses normal rendering.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise the pure append predicate with accepted ASCII and rejected cursor, placeholder, multiline, wrap-boundary, Vietnamese, combining-mark, CJK, emoji, control, NBSP, and Latin-1 cases.

candidate_atomics.name: gate-direct-backspace-by-safe-terminal-grapheme
candidate_atomics.title: Restrict direct terminal backspace to ASCII graphemes
candidate_atomics.description: Permit the one-cell terminal erase shortcut only when the final removed grapheme is printable ASCII and the edit occurs at the end of a nonempty single-line value.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid clearing the wrong number or composition state of terminal cells when deleting Unicode graphemes through a one-cell stdout shortcut.
semantic_action.module_role: terminal text-input deletion fast-path eligibility owner
semantic_action.pre_state: A direct backspace escape sequence is allowed for any final grapheme measured as one display cell, including non-ASCII or composed graphemes whose renderer state may not be safely updated by a one-cell erase.
semantic_action.post_state: The direct one-cell erase is eligible only for a final printable-ASCII grapheme at the end of nonempty single-line input under the existing TTY fast-path conditions; other deletions use normal rendering.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise the pure backspace predicate with an accepted trailing ASCII character and rejected non-terminal cursor, empty deletion, multiline, Vietnamese, CJK, decomposed-combining, and emoji cases.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-terminal-fast-path-boundary
candidate_atomics.title: Validate the optimized and renderer fallback boundaries
candidate_atomics.description: Encode a regression matrix proving that ordinary ASCII remains eligible while Unicode, composition-sensitive, control, multiline, cursor-position, and wrapping cases are routed away from direct terminal echo.

semantic_action.intent: Make the terminal fast-path safety boundary observable and prevent future broadening based only on display width.
semantic_action.module_role: terminal input fast-path contract test owner
semantic_action.pre_state: Fast-path eligibility is embedded in component-local logic and lacks focused coverage distinguishing safe ASCII edits from unsafe Unicode and layout cases.
semantic_action.post_state: Pure eligibility predicates have a focused regression oracle covering positive ASCII behavior and negative Unicode and structural boundaries for both append and backspace.
semantic_action.validation: Run the dedicated fast-echo test suite and require every positive and negative eligibility expectation to pass; compare against the parent guard when establishing regression sensitivity.

candidate_workflows.name: harden-terminal-direct-echo-boundary
candidate_workflows.title: Make a terminal input fast path safe for Unicode and IME text
candidate_workflows.description: Identify the direct-render bypass, define a conservative text-and-layout contract for each optimized edit, preserve the safe ASCII path, and validate both eligibility and fallback boundaries with pure regression tests.

workflow_graph.goal: Keep terminal-rendered value, cells, and cursor position synchronized for Unicode and composition-based input without removing the direct-echo optimization for safe ASCII edits.
when_to_use: A terminal input component writes append or erase sequences directly to the terminal and bypasses its normal renderer.
Unicode or IME input produces duplicated, scattered, ghosted, incorrectly erased, or cursor-desynchronized text.
Existing fast-path eligibility relies mainly on code-unit length or display-width equality.
anti_goals: Do not disable the optimization for ordinary printable ASCII edits that satisfy the existing TTY and layout constraints.
Do not treat display width alone as proof that an edit is safe to render outside the normal renderer.
Do not redesign Unicode segmentation, the normal rendering engine, or the input method implementation when a conservative bypass boundary resolves the fault.
not_applicable_when: The component has no direct-to-terminal rendering bypass and all edits already pass through the layout renderer.
The defect is inside the normal renderer's width, wrapping, or grapheme calculation rather than in bypass eligibility.
The required optimized path must support composition-aware non-ASCII input and the system provides a proven composition protocol rather than a conservative fallback.
inputs: The direct append and deletion call sites
Runtime conditions controlling direct terminal output
Current value, cursor, terminal width, and rendered line width
Representative ASCII, composed, combining, wide, emoji, control, multiline, and wrapping cases
workflow_graph.entry_state: A direct terminal edit path can be selected for text whose measured width appears compatible even though its Unicode or composition behavior cannot safely bypass full rendering.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Only explicitly safe printable-ASCII end-of-line edits use direct terminal writes; unsafe text and layouts fall back to normal rendering, and focused tests pin both the retained optimization and rejected cases.

steps.condition: A direct append shortcut writes inserted text without a normal renderer pass.
steps.validation: The append predicate accepts safe printable ASCII below the wrap boundary and rejects all covered Unicode, composition-sensitive, control, cursor, placeholder, multiline, and wrapping cases.

steps.condition: A direct erase shortcut assumes that deleting the previous grapheme can be represented by a fixed one-cell terminal sequence.
steps.validation: The backspace predicate accepts deletion of a final ASCII character and rejects Unicode graphemes and structurally unsafe deletion states.

steps.condition: The optimized append or backspace path remains present after tightening eligibility.
steps.validation: The dedicated predicate suite passes and demonstrates both preservation of eligible ASCII behavior and fallback for unsafe input classes.

validation_ladder: Inspect the direct stdout call sites and confirm failed eligibility continues into the normal edit/render flow.
Unit-test the pure append predicate across safe ASCII, cursor, placeholder, multiline, wrap, Unicode, combining, wide, emoji, and control cases.
Unit-test the pure backspace predicate across safe ASCII and unsafe cursor, empty, multiline, composed, combining, wide, and emoji cases.
Run the focused suite against the prior eligibility logic to establish that the matrix detects the regression, then run it against the new logic for green results.
Where an interactive terminal and relevant input method are available, manually verify composition and deletion without doubled or ghosted cells.
stop_conditions: Stop if no renderer-bypassing terminal write can be identified; this workflow does not apply.
Stop and investigate the normal renderer if unsafe cases still fail after being routed away from the bypass.
Do not broaden the fast path beyond the tested printable-ASCII contract without an independently validated composition- and cell-aware protocol.
Do not claim end-to-end IME correctness from predicate tests alone.
unresolved_or_deferred: No automated end-to-end terminal/IME integration test was added; the committed tests validate pure eligibility decisions.
The extraction did not execute the test suite in a worktree at the pinned ref; green/red results are reported by the commit message, while the test oracle itself is directly inspectable.
The test source contains 19 individual test blocks although the commit message describes 20 cases, likely counting multiple assertions or matrix entries rather than test blocks.

unresolved_questions: Whether all supported terminals and input methods expose composition events in the same way remains unverified by the focused predicate tests.
The repository bundle lacks PR discussion, review, and status-check metadata, so validation beyond the checkout and author-reported commit message is unavailable.
